b2-25-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Promise to Call
b2-25-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you to call her when you arrive. You promise that you will not forget.
b2-25-01.prompt: Promise Meg that you will call her when you arrive.
cues: Promise that you will call her
b2-25-01.target: No te preocupes: no dejaré de llamarte cuando llegue.
b2-25-01.english: Do not worry: I will be sure to call you when I arrive.
b2-25-01.canDo: I can use *dejar de* + infinitive for things that stop and *no dejes de* for "be sure to".

b2-25-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Just Arrived
b2-25-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos phones and asks where you are. You have just arrived at the station and you will wait for him at the entrance.
b2-25-02.prompt: Tell Carlos where you are and where you will wait.
cues: Say that you have just arrived
Say where you will wait for him
b2-25-02.target: Acabo de llegar a la estación. Te espero en la entrada.
b2-25-02.english: I have just arrived at the station. I will wait for you at the entrance.
b2-25-02.canDo: I can use *acabar de* for what has just happened and *acababa de* for the scene behind a story.

b2-25-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of the Meeting
b2-25-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the meeting ended. There was a long discussion, and in the end everyone accepted the plan.
b2-25-03.prompt: Tell Meg how the meeting ended.
cues: Say that the discussion was long
Say that everyone finally accepted the plan
b2-25-03.target: Después de una larga discusión, todos terminaron por aceptar el plan.
b2-25-03.english: After a long discussion, everyone ended up accepting the plan.
b2-25-03.canDo: I can use *terminar por* and *acabar por* + infinitive for what happens in the end.

b2-25-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Tired Day
b2-25-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you look tired. Yesterday you were so tired that you even fell asleep in class.
b2-25-04.prompt: Tell Carlos why you look tired.
cues: Say what you even did in class
b2-25-04.target: Estaba tan cansada que llegué a dormirme en la clase.
b2-25-04.english: I was so tired that I even fell asleep in class.
b2-25-04.canDo: I can use *llegar a* + infinitive for getting as far as doing something.

b2-25-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lost Keys
b2-25-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your keys. You looked for them all day and then gave them up for lost.
b2-25-05.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to your keys.
cues: Say that you looked for them all day
Say that you gave them up for lost
b2-25-05.target: Después de buscar todo el día, di por perdidas las llaves.
b2-25-05.english: After looking all day, I gave the keys up for lost.
b2-25-05.canDo: I can use *dar por* + participle to treat something as finished, lost or certain.

b2-25-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Way Home
b2-25-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how your trip home was. You have just arrived home. You stopped waiting for the bus and in the end you went on foot.
b2-25-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos about your trip home.
cues: Say that you have just arrived
Say that you stopped waiting for the bus
Say that in the end you went on foot
b2-25-consolidation.target: Acabo de llegar a casa. Dejé de esperar el autobús y terminé por ir a pie.
b2-25-consolidation.english: I have just arrived home. I stopped waiting for the bus and ended up going on foot.
b2-25-consolidation.canDo: I can choose between *dejar de*, *acabar de*, *terminar por*, *llegar a* and *dar por*.
